text:
incident-bot: Incident created: gpu-node-42 ECC spike -> P2. Pager: @ajay. Details: gpu.ecc.errors increased from 2 to 18 in 7m on gpu-3 (node-42).

maria: seeing repeated pages from this node for the last 2 nights around 02:00 UTC. possibly correlated with nightly tensor-dump job. paging noise is getting noisy.

ajay: taking it. i'm oncall now, looking at metrics. can someone confirm customer impact?

monitoring-bot: alert triggered: gpu.ecc.error.count > 10 in 10m on node-42 (rule id: gpu-ecc-10m).

leo: quick check - thermal graphs spike ~5-8C at the same time. DC HVAC schedule shows cooling cycle at ~01:50 UTC as well. could be ambient-related + job load.

ophelia: i also see VRAM growth on the model worker on gpu-3. probably a mem leak in nightly job causing retries and elevated error counts. not sure it's ECC causing failures or just exposing underlying stress.

jess: customer support: a few latency spikes and a small set of intermittent 503s for embeddings endpoints between 02:05-02:20 UTC, ~3 customers. not widespread.

ajay: plan: cordon node-42, migrate pods off GPU-3, run quick memory leak capture, and hold off full node drain until we confirm ECC severity. cordon -> evict small batch -> monitor.

maria: +1 to cordon. but we also need to reduce noisy pages while we investigate. current alerting thresholds are too brittle for transient ECC flaps.

ajay: agree. proposing immediate temporary changes:
- suppress repeat ECC page for 30m while we recover node (auto-suppress on rule id gpu-ecc-10m)
- change ECC alert semantics to rate-based: alert on sustained increase over 1h instead of 10m absolute count
- only page for node-drain if eviction fails or OOM/kubelet reports critical.

ophelia: can you paste the proposed Prometheus alert snippet? want to review semantics.

ajay: sure:
```
- alert: GPU_ECC_Rate_High
  expr: increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[1h]) > 5 and increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[1h]) / on(node) gpu_attached_gpus > 0.5
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained ECC error rate on {{ $labels.node }}"
```

leo: switch to corrected Ecc counters is good (less noisy). also add a "for: 15m" to avoid short flaps. rate normalization by GPU count is 👍.

maria: for VRAM alerts i suggest changing threshold from 92% (instant) to 95% sustained for 5m, and add a panel to the infra dashboard showing per-GPU VRAM delta over 1h to spot slow leaks.

monitoring-bot: proposed alert change created in draft: alert/prometheus/rules/gpu_ecc_rate.yml (PR pending).

jess: are we going to update pagerduty escalation? i want first pager to be oncall, then platform lead if not acked in 10m.

ajay: yes — no change to PD policy now, but we'll add a short suppression window on the specific rule to avoid duplicate escalations.

ophelia: during cordon i'm going to disable nightly tensor-dump for node-42 via the job tag override to avoid repeating the pattern.

maria: action items summarized:
- ajay: cordon node-42, migrate pods, run heap capture on model worker, follow up with logs (ETA 20m)
- ajay: land temporary alert suppression + rate-based ECC rule (draft PR linked) (ETA 1h)
- leo: add VRAM delta panel and GPU thermals per rack to the infra dashboard + tag maintenance window for 01:45-02:15 (ETA EOD)
- ophelia: disable nightly tensor-dump on node-42 for next run and open issue for memory leak (INC-1234)
- jess: update support note for affected customers with ETA 2h

ajay: performing cordon now: `kubectl cordon node-42` -> `kubectl drain node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`

monitoring-bot: node-42 cordoned, pod evictions started.

maria: watching health endpoints. p99 latency back to baseline so far. no new 503s in last 6m.

ajay: eviction completed for most pods. one model-worker pod crashed during eviction (OOM) — that's likely where VRAM leak is. leaving node cordoned for deeper analysis.

ophelia: started heapdump capture of the crashed worker and uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/gpu-node-42/heapdumps/ (link: https://s3.internal/...).

maria: follow-up alerting decisions (post-incident):
- make GPU ECC alert rate-based and normalized by GPU count (as ajay proto'd)
- add 10m suppression window immediately after any manual cordon/drain to avoid duplicate pages from transient eviction failures
- change node-drain paging to only page when `kube_eviction_failures_total` > 0 after 5m or if kubelet reports critical events (OOM, kernel panic)
- create a dashboard tab "GPU Health - Forensics" with: VRAM delta 1h, ECC corrected/unexpected counts, thermal 5m moving avg, and pod evictions timeline.

leo: will create dashboard PR and include annotation panel to mark scheduled DC HVAC cycles. might explain repeated thermal upticks.

ajay: creating follow-up runbook PR to capture the above. linking to ticket INC-1234 and will add checklists for cordon/drain and safe alert suppression steps.

jess: i'll ping customers with summary and will update when we have root cause.

incident-bot: Incident gpu-node-42 ECC spike -> acknowledged by ajay. status: mitigated (cordoned) — follow-ups created: INC-1234, PR#3456 (alerts), PR#3457 (dashboard), runbook PR#3458.

maria: thanks team. we'll review RCA once heapdump analysis completes. for now let's keep the temporary suppression for 30m and monitor. :thumbsup:
